items.followUp: A machine takes in 800 J of energy and gives 600 J of useful output. Find its efficiency.

rubric.why: Identifies useful output and total input as the quantities compared.
rubric.description: State that efficiency compares useful output with total input.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the output-to-input ratio.

rubric.why: The efficiency is expressed as a percentage.
rubric.description: Give the efficiency formula as a percentage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the ratio multiplied by 100.

modelAnswer: Efficiency is the ratio of useful output energy to total input energy, expressed as a percentage.
Efficiency = (useful output energy / total input energy) × 100%.

rubric.why: Stress is defined as force acting per unit area.
rubric.description: Define stress.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for force per unit area or its formula.

rubric.why: Strain is the fractional change in length and has no unit.
rubric.description: Define strain and distinguish it from stress.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the change-to-original-length ratio; no unit is also acceptable as the distinction.

modelAnswer: Stress is the force acting per unit area of a body: stress = F/A.
Strain is the change in length divided by the original length: strain = ΔL/L.
Stress has the unit pascal (Pa), while strain has no unit.

items.followUp: Using a velocity-time graph, derive the equation v_f² = v_i² + 2as.

rubric.why: The proof uses a velocity-time graph with initial and final velocities over time t.
rubric.description: Draw or describe the velocity-time graph and label its quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correctly labelled graph or equivalent description.

rubric.why: The area under a velocity-time graph represents displacement.
rubric.description: Relate the area under the graph to displacement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the graph area equals displacement.

rubric.why: The area consists of a rectangle and a triangle.
rubric.description: Write the rectangle-plus-triangle area expression.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for s = v_i t + 1/2(v_f − v_i)t or equivalent.

rubric.why: Using a = (v_f − v_i)/t gives the required result.
rubric.description: Substitute the acceleration relation and obtain the required equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct substitution and final equation.

modelAnswer: Draw a velocity-time graph: time t on the horizontal axis, velocity on the vertical axis, starting at v_i and ending at v_f.
Displacement s equals the area under the graph.
The area is a rectangle plus a triangle: s = v_i t + 1/2 (v_f − v_i)t.
Since a = (v_f − v_i)/t, then v_f − v_i = at.
Therefore, s = v_i t + 1/2 at².

items.followUp: A body of mass 20 kg is raised to a height of 5 m. Find its potential energy, taking g = 10 m/s².

rubric.why: The mass, height and gravitational acceleration are identified in SI units.
rubric.description: Write the given data, including g.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct data; accept g = 9.8 m/s² if used consistently.

rubric.why: Gravitational potential energy is mass times gravitational acceleration times height.
rubric.description: Select the potential-energy formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for PE = mgh.

rubric.why: The values must be substituted into the formula.
rubric.description: Substitute the given values with units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution.

rubric.why: The arithmetic gives 1500 J for g = 10, or 1470 J for g = 9.8.
rubric.description: Calculate the potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct numerical value for the chosen g.

rubric.why: Energy must be reported in joules.
rubric.description: State the answer with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer and unit.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 50 kg, h = 3 m, g = 10 m/s².
Formula: PE = mgh.
Substitution: PE = 50 kg × 10 m/s² × 3 m.
PE = 1500 kg·m²/s².
Potential energy = 1500 J.

items.followUp: Define Young's modulus and derive its equation in terms of force, area, original length and extension.

rubric.why: Young's modulus is defined as the ratio of stress to strain within the elastic limit.
rubric.description: Give the definition of Young's modulus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the ratio and elastic-limit condition.

rubric.why: Stress is force divided by cross-sectional area.
rubric.description: Write the stress relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stress = F/A.

rubric.why: Strain is extension divided by original length.
rubric.description: Write the strain relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct strain expression.

rubric.why: Substituting stress and strain gives the required equation.
rubric.description: Derive Young's modulus equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Y = FL/(AΔL), or the equivalent derivation.

modelAnswer: Young's modulus is the ratio of stress to strain within the elastic limit.
Stress = force / cross-sectional area = F/A.
Strain = extension / original length = ΔL/L.
Y = stress / strain = (F/A) / (ΔL/L).
Therefore, Y = FL/(AΔL).

items.followUp: Convert 12 years into seconds, taking 1 year = 365 days.

rubric.why: The year-to-second conversion uses days, hours and seconds.
rubric.description: State the time conversion factors.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct conversion factors.

rubric.why: Multiplying the conversion factors gives the duration in seconds.
rubric.description: Calculate and state the age in seconds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 504,576,000 s or an equivalent value.

modelAnswer: Given: 16 years; 1 year = 365 days, 1 day = 24 hours, 1 hour = 3600 s.
Therefore, 16 years = 5.04576 × 10⁸ s.

items.followUp: Write the names of four fundamental SI units.

rubric.why: Any two correct derived-unit names earn this mark.
rubric.description: Name two derived units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two correct examples.

rubric.why: The question asks for four derived units; common examples include newton, joule, pascal and watt.
rubric.description: Name the remaining derived units to give four examples.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for completing four correct examples overall.

modelAnswer: Four derived units are the newton (N), joule (J), pascal (Pa) and watt (W).

items.followUp: Define velocity and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Acceleration is the rate at which velocity changes with time.
rubric.description: Define acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for change in velocity per unit time.

rubric.why: The SI unit of acceleration is metre per second squared.
rubric.description: Write the SI unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for m/s².

modelAnswer: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time: a = change in velocity / time.
Its SI unit is metre per second squared (m/s²).
